verdict: Quiet follow-through day after major Sept 30 bull cluster (AVGO Q3 beat, MU Q4 earnings); only fresh Oct 1 item is Cantor NVDA reaffirm; underlying AI/HBM thesis intact, CPO inflection on schedule.
body_md:
## Fresh Developments (Last 24–72h)

**Signal 1 – DRAM/HBM Pricing:** No new 24-72h pricing print. Prior TrendForce data confirms Q3 server DRAM contract prices +13–18% QoQ — pace decelerating from Q1's +90–95% and Q2's +58–63%, but direction still up. Spot HBM3E ~$2,100 (~5x the $350–400 LTA price); extreme spread holds.

**Signal 2 – HBM4 Ramp/Correction Risk:** No new 24-72h data. Most recent: Micron targeting 100K HBM wafers/month by year-end (from ~40–50K; TrendForce Sept 4). All three suppliers expanding at pace — baseline post-2026 correction risk continues to build.

**Signal 3 – Hyperscaler AI Capex:** No new 24-72h print. Last Q2 guidance: combined big-4 ~$730B for 2026 (Amazon $220B, Google $195–205B, Microsoft ~$175B, Meta $130–145B). Above the baseline $600–700B range; no guide-down detected. **Freshest item (Oct 1):** Cantor Fitzgerald reiterates NVDA Overweight / $350 PT.

**Signal 4 – AMD MI400/Helios + Custom ASICs:** No new 24-72h catalyst. AMD Helios rack-scale (72 MI455X GPUs, 31 TB HBM4, 1.7 PB/s) confirmed in 2H-2026 shipment. Google TPU v8, AWS Trainium 3, Meta MTIA all on prior schedule.

**Signal 5 – Optical/Photonics:** No new 24-72h catalyst beyond what was noted in prior runs. COHR PhotonLink platform (Sept 21) in 10+ CPO customer engagements; Q4 CY2026 revenue ramp guided. LITE multi-hundred-million CPO laser order on track. 2026 is first year of CPO volume deployment — thesis playing out.

**Signal 6 – Solar:** No new 24-72h news. Section 232 tariffs (effective Dec 4, 2026) set $0.38/W module floor / $21/kg polysilicon floor — FSLR remains structural beneficiary as domestic CdTe producer. BMO targets US module prices ~$0.43–0.44/W post-Dec 4.

**Signal 7 – Watchlist:** See table below.

---

## Watchlist Movers

| Name | Move | Catalyst |
|------|------|----------|
| **NVDA** | Analyst reaffirm | Cantor Fitzgerald reiterates Overweight / $350 PT, Oct 1 — only confirmed fresh note today |
| **MU** | Oct 1 reaction | Q4 FY2026 results released Sept 30 after close; Q1 FY2027 guide ~$50B ±$1B, ~86% GM — market digesting today |
| **COHR** | Recent catalyst | PhotonLink CPO platform launch Sept 21; 10+ customer engagements; Q4 revenue ramp starting |
| **HIVE** | Prior catalyst | $350M 5-yr GPU cloud deal (2,016 NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GB300, Aug 17); BUZZ HPC ARR ~$180M |

*No notable fresh movers in ALAB, CRDO, CIEN, LITE, FSLR, ENPH, NXT, ARRY, AMD, AVGO, MRVL, STX, WDC, SNDK, RMBS, MRAM, NOW, ZS, CRM, SNOW, TSLA, GDDY, NOK, AMPX, ALMU in last 24h.*

---

## Context vs Baseline

- Hyperscaler capex ~$730B is now above the baseline $600–700B range — bull case exceeded.
- MU Q1 FY2027 guide of ~$50B at ~86% GM (if confirmed) would represent continued HBM/DRAM pricing power well into 2027 — directly challenges the baseline correction-risk timeline.
- CPO entering volume deployment in Q4 CY2026 is on schedule with baseline expectation; first commercial COHR revenue is the key watch.
- All three HBM suppliers at full expansion pace — baseline correction-risk signal post-2026 remains the most important tail risk to watch into Q1 2027 earnings commentary.

---

## Signals Flashing

| Signal | Direction | Bull/Bear |
|--------|-----------|-----------|
| DRAM/HBM spot-contract spread | Extreme premium holding | Bull (near-term, MU/RMBS) |
| HBM4 capacity build (all 3 suppliers) | Accelerating | Bear (post-2026 correction risk) |
| Hyperscaler capex ($730B, no guide-down) | Above plan | Bull (NVDA, MRVL, ALAB, CRDO) |
| MU Q1 FY2027 guide (~$50B, ~86% GM) | Strong | Bull |
| CPO inflection (COHR, LITE) | Revenue ramp beginning Q4 | Bull |
| Section 232 solar tariffs (Dec 4 effective) | Domestic production benefit | Bull (FSLR) |

---

## Most Important Development

**Today (Oct 1) is quiet** — a follow-through day after a major bull catalyst cluster on Sept 30 (AVGO Q3 beat + MU Q4 earnings). The only confirmed fresh item is Cantor's NVDA reaffirm. The key watch for the rest of this week is MU's stock reaction to its Q4 FY2026 results and Q1 FY2027 guidance ($50B, 86% GM), which will set the tone for the broader AI/HBM memory complex entering Q4 2026. The correction-risk signal (all three HBM suppliers completing expansions) remains the most important bearish tail risk and will crystallize in 2027 earnings guidance commentary.
